notes.text: The page is a typed letter addressed to Verdier, dated Massy le 18.5.1971. It ends with a question and has no closing or signature on this leaf. The lower-left handwritten 14 is recorded as archival numbering.
notes.basis: Observation: date, salutation, last body line and lower-left margin.

notes.text: The writer says he has no time for the reissue of SGA 4. Saavedra has helped with an index for Chap IV, par.9 à 13. Progress is blocked pending two Deligne appendices, described literally as assez, de points and image inverse d’un plat; he asks whether Verdier has them and can send them for typing.
notes.basis: Observation: paragraph 1, lines 1–7. This records the letter’s statements, not independently established publication history.

notes.text: He asks for a corrected version of exercise 4.10.6, labelled médaille chocolat, and says he has forgotten what was canulé. The word entièrement has a clipped ending. He says the exercise is continually useful and asks for something true to replace the false material; no replacement or proof is given here.
notes.basis: Observation: paragraph 1, lines 8–13; clip checked in crop 03. No mathematical proof check was performed.

notes.text: If Verdier is tired of final preparation of SGA 4, the writer wants instructions and is willing to leave it incomplet et dégueulasse rather than spend one or two days away from boulot survie. He asks about Artin’s wishes for the exposés after VI and whether to send his bundle of errata, footnotes and improvements.
notes.basis: Observation: paragraph 2; this summarizes requests and priorities stated on the page.

notes.text: The two component pairs o/l and e/apostrophe are read from visible contours, without using grammar to assign strike order. The complete page reading preserves both orders. The faint backwards line above/behind the date is treated as a reverse impression, not additional forward-facing letter text. H’s opening editorial note is not transcribed as source prose.
notes.basis: Observation: crops 04–05 and whole/half-a upper margin; inference limited to classifying the faint reversed impression.

notes.text: No mathematical checking, re-proof or computation occurred in this run. Transcription and visual collation alone do not establish the mathematical claims. TeX spacing and line wrapping, ellipsis syntax and the witnesses’ ways of encoding prose dashes are not counted as textual differences.
notes.basis: Scope of this reader run; check_events deliberately empty.
